page: Amazon Web Services r6g.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors. The system delivers 64 physical cores (64 vCPUs) based on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It provides direct, non-virtualized access to hardware, supported by 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory configured at an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local storage is not included, requiring external network block storage for persistence. High-throughput network communication is sustained by a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not present on this bare-metal platform.

Benchmark results demonstrate high throughput across parallel computational tasks and memory operations. The instance achieved 97,247.25 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 73.76 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, placing both in the top tier. Compilation workflows also scale effectively, reaching 44,264.0 in Clang build benchmarks, while static web serving reached 47.29 GB/sec. Cached small-block memory reads performed at 3,792.76 GB/sec. In contrast, single-threaded processing reflects architectural limitations of the Neoverse-N1 cores at 2.5 GHz, scoring 985.0 on single-core Geekbench and 1,522.9 on single-core stress-ng tests. Large language model token generation was similarly constrained, producing 2.33 tokens per second on 70B parameter models and 8.51 tokens per second on 135M parameter models.

From an efficiency perspective, the Graviton2 processor architecture yields high thread-level throughput and high memory density per core without hyperthreading overhead. Cost efficiency is optimized for software natively compiled for arm64 that relies on distributed memory footprints and high parallel capacity. However, the absence of integrated local NVMe storage and discrete acceleration hardware makes the platform reliant on attached network volumes and unsuitable for GPU-dependent deep learning pipelines. Workloads well matched to r6g.metal include large-scale in-memory key-value caches like Redis, distributed relational and non-relational database engines, real-time analytics platforms, Clang build farms, and memory-intensive container platforms that benefit from non-virtualized hardware access.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores running on the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 (Neoverse-N1) processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it yields an 8:1 memory-to-core balance suitable for data-intensive footprints. The hardware provides bare-metal execution without a hypervisor layer, 25 Gbps baseline networking, zero discrete GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, r6g.metal excels in parallelized workloads, delivering strong throughput in Redis SET operations (73.76M ops/sec), multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, and Clang software compilation, alongside 47.29 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-threaded metrics and LLM autoregressive generation tests register modest results, aligning performance characteristics with high-concurrency tasks. This instance is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-density container hosts, and parallel data processing jobs requiring direct access to physical memory.
